correctness.rationale: In the fixed-norm lossy dimer with 0<Gamma<J and equal g/(1+|psi_j|²) nonlinearities, writing imbalance s=|psi1|²-|psi2|² and relative phase gives sin(phi)=Gamma sqrt(1-s²)/J, so precisely two phase branches exist. Their exact detuning functions are delta_±(s)=2g s/(9-s²)±F(s), F(s)=s sqrt[J²/(1-s²)-Gamma²]. The plus branch is a bijective strictly increasing map R to R. The negative branch derivative =2(9+s²)/(9-s²)² [g-R(s²)], and exact log derivative inequalities make R strictly increasing from g_c=(9/2)sqrt(J²-Gamma²) to infinity. Thus for g<=gc there is one negative branch crossing everywhere (total 2); for g>gc one pair of folds and negative branch has 3,2,1 intersections by detuning, giving total 4,3,2. Cubic Taylor of negative branch at s=0 proves a nondegenerate cusp width proportional to (g-gc)^(3/2), with coefficient [8/(27 sqrt3)]sqrt(sqrt(J²-Gamma²)/(7J²+2Gamma²)); as g->infinity s*->1 and delta*/g->1/4. No claims about dynamics or linear exceptional points.
